page.layout: One page of text, one column of verse. Running head at the top centre, page number at the top left. The catchword sits alone at the lower right.

main_text.p: Præripit humanæ, sibi debita præmia laudi: Sic olim Pharij currúsque, virósque tyranni Gurgitibus mersos, retro & dilapsa referri Æquora, ut effugeret, mirata est turba piorum. Præsenti sic se miratus & ipse ruinæ Ereptum Ezechias, aduersáque castra perire Angelica vastante manu. Sic cara Deo gens Iuratum pendere hostem conspexit Amanum, Vltrix ipsa sui: cum se se ostenderet ante Sola mali facies, & plurima mortis Imago.

Nos ergo quibus hæc præstas, Rex maxime, soli Deberi hanc laudem, tibi grata mente fatemur. Solius ista tua est, tua Christe, hæc dextera nostra Imbelles timidæque manus: adstrenua surda Aures consilia, atque aufis[?] mens talibus impar, Ni face succensa attonitas tua gratia mentes Excitet, atque animos inspires ipse viriles. Crediderunt nec vana fides, de millibus unum Angelicis, tua quæ castra & tua iussa sequuntur Demissum cælo hos animos fecisse repente Henrico, ut sanctas faceres hæc otia genti. O gentem felicem, ô térque quatérque beatam. Quæ te voce pia Dominúmque Deúmque fatetur, Et sentit, totámque in te spem cauta reponit. Illa etenim vultus radiis lustrata sereni Te tribuente capit pietatis præmia, & eius Continuata pium diffundunt Gaudia pectus.
Perge igitur, nec cœpta sine hæc miracula finem

page.notes: The text is set as one continuous verse passage; the stanza breaks are not visible as gaps, so the verse is given as paragraphs at the visible indents. "aufis" is read as printed and may be "auris" (marked [?]). The line "mi ratus" has a gap in the print, read as "miratus". The lines of the page are verse lines printed in italic type with no italics marked, as the type is roman with long s. The catchword "Accipere" is taken from the lower right.
